newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power falls amid flat demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power falls amid flat demand.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were steady Wednesday versus Tuesday's levels amid flat demand for electricity in the region, market sources said.
"Load is just flat," said a Southeast trader, due to normal September weather in the region.
"We saw prices moved down by a dollar," said a Houston trader. "We expect prices to fall again tomorrow."

In the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC), non-firm power for heavy-load hours on Thursday delivered into the northern portion of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) was discussed in the $14.75-$15.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range, flat from Tuesday's level.
Electricity in the southern part of the TVA was valued in the $17.00-$17.50.
Electricity prices for non-firm, peak delivery into the Florida/Georgia border on Thursday were valued at $20.50-$21.00, down from Tuesday's $21.00-$21.50 range.
Transmission capacity to move power into Florida from other regions within SERC remained tight because of seasonal demand and outages of a couple of large generation units, traders said.

The 900 megawatt (MW) Scherer coal-fired unit 4 in Juliette, Ga., was shut Monday for seasonal maintenance, and was scheduled to return to service at the end of October, the operator Georgia Power Co said.
Florida Power Corp's 825 MW Crystal River 3 nuclear unit in Red Level. Fla., remained shut following repairs to a leaky section of line that feeds lubrication oil to the unit's turbine shaft.
